description: Elizabeth Bennet and the proud Mr. Darcy misjudge each other in a witty portrait of class, marriage and first impressions in Regency England.
A young scientist creates life and then abandons it, with tragic results. One of the first science-fiction novels, and still one of the most chilling.
Twelve cases of the world's most famous detective, told by Dr. Watson: disguises, blackmail, a speckled band and the Red-Headed League.
Alice follows a white rabbit down a hole into a world of riddles, croquet with flamingos and a very unreasonable Queen.
Captain Ahab's obsessive hunt for the white whale, narrated by the sailor Ishmael, is part adventure, part meditation on fate and the sea.
Told through letters, diaries and news clippings, Count Dracula's arrival in England sets a band of friends against an ancient evil.
A beautiful young man stays unchanged while his portrait ages and records every sin. Wilde's only novel is a dark tale of vanity and corruption.
London and Paris on the eve of the French Revolution, and a story of sacrifice: 'It was the best of times, it was the worst of times.'
An orphaned governess with a fierce sense of independence falls for her brooding employer, and discovers the secret hidden at Thornfield Hall.
On the Yorkshire moors, Heathcliff and Catherine's wild, destructive love reaches across two generations.
A poor student murders a pawnbroker and is hunted by his own conscience in Dostoevsky's psychological masterpiece.
Huck and the runaway Jim drift down the Mississippi on a raft, in a sharp, funny look at friendship and freedom in the American South.
Mischief, buried treasure and a murder witnessed in a graveyard fill a boyhood summer in a small Mississippi town.
A Victorian inventor travels to the year 802,701 and finds humanity split into two very different species.
Martian war machines land in Surrey and begin to destroy everything in their path. The founding story of alien invasion.
Captain Nemo and his submarine Nautilus take three captives on a tour of the ocean's wonders and terrors.

match: around the world in eighty days
description: Phileas Fogg bets his fortune that he can circle the globe in eighty days, and a detective is on his trail.
Young Jim Hawkins, a map, and Long John Silver: the original pirate adventure.
A respectable doctor's experiment releases the cruel Mr. Hyde. A short, tense study of the double life within us all.
Confined to a room for her 'rest cure', a woman becomes fixated on the pattern of the wallpaper. A landmark of feminist literature.
Machiavelli's famous guide to winning and keeping power, practical, cold and still argued over five centuries later.
The private notes of the Roman emperor Marcus Aurelius on duty, discipline and staying calm.
Three ghosts visit the miser Ebenezer Scrooge on Christmas Eve and show him the cost of his choices.
Swift's savage satire proposes a shocking solution to Irish poverty. One of the most famous essays in English.
Lemuel Gulliver visits lands of tiny people, giants and talking horses in Swift's biting satire of human folly.
Gregor Samsa wakes up as an enormous insect. Kafka's strange, short story of alienation and family.
The boy who wouldn't grow up takes Wendy and her brothers to Neverland, to Captain Hook's ship and back.
A Kansas farm girl is swept to the Land of Oz and sets off down the yellow brick road to find the Wizard.
The four March sisters grow up in Civil War New England: Meg, Jo, Beth and Amy.
Buck, a pampered dog, is stolen and sent to the Yukon gold rush, where he must find the wolf inside.
Odysseus's ten-year journey home from Troy, in the epic poem that started adventure storytelling (Samuel Butler's prose translation).
Two young lovers from feuding families in Verona. Shakespeare's most famous tragedy.
